title: National Emergency Medical Services Memorial Extension Act
official_summary:
National Emergency Medical Services Memorial Extension Act

This bill reauthorizes the National Emergency Medical Services Memorial Foundation to establish in Washington, DC, a monument to commemorate the commitment and service represented by emergency medical services. This authorization expires seven years after enactment of the bill.

summary.headline: Congress gives a private foundation more time to build a memorial in Washington, DC, honoring emergency medical services workers.
summary.what_it_does: This law renews the National Emergency Medical Services Memorial Foundation's permission to build a monument in Washington, DC, honoring the service of emergency medical services. The new permission lasts seven years from the date the law was enacted.
summary.when_it_takes_effect: Took effect when signed on September 11, 2026; the permission to build the memorial expires seven years later, around September 11, 2033.
